pr_title: Make IgnoreNullValues apply only to reference types
pr_body:
- Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/38800 (a regression from 3.1)
- Adds logic to honor IgnoreNullValues to ctor args

issue_context.title: System.Text.Json: IgnoreNullValues ignores field that have a default value
comments:
This commit might be the root cause: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/c2291eb865fa542c888cefdb16e669dceffeda5f#diff-6945dba66187c255555ac8232ef4584dR140

See how it added that with Options.IgnoreNullValues we ignore the default values on read/write.
While that is correct for reference types, it's not the case for value types.

From that commit I see that IgnoreNullValues has been obsoleted, replaced by DefaultIgnoreCondition.
Still I believe that:
- existing code should still work as it used to
- we still need to differentiate serialization of null from default value, these have very different semantic in Javascript (which is  the target of that serializer)

From the mentioned commit:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5130190/86589014-1c0b0680-bf8d-11ea-9f56-0efae610d108.png)
I think that WhenNull should be kept as an option, which would have the same effect as obsolete Options.IgnoreNullValues.
Most likely most folks will want that behaviour.
